texts.facts: The petitioner filed this petition U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1988 claiming compensation from the respondents due to injuries sustained in a road traffic accident. 2. Brief facts of petitioner's case is that on 03.10.2022 at about 01.45 p.m, the petitioner was traveling in KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-3773, on Kolar-Bangalore NH Road, when the bus reached opposite to NH-75 Hotel, near Mylapura Gate Hosakote, Bangalore Rural District, the driver of said bus drove the same in a rash and negligent manner so as to endangering to human life and dashed to one Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16/D-9498, which was parked on the road by its driver without any precaution, as a result of forced impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries. 3. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Silicon City Hospital for first aid, and further shifted to Raksha Hospital, wherein, she took treatment as inpatient and undergone surgery and spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical expenses, food, transportation, conveyance and other charges. Due to the said accidental injuries, the petitioner completely bed ridden, cannot run, jump, cannot lift or carry any weight, unable to sleep properly, she cannot do his activities as earlier to the accident and undergoing deep mental shock, pain and suffering, since the injuries caused permanent in nature. Pushpa vs K.S.R.T.C on 27 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29361503/ 2 4. It is contended that, this accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-3773 and also due to negligence on the part of the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16/D- 9498. Hence, the Hosakote Police have registered a case against drivers of said vehicles in crime No.353/2022. 5. It is contended that, prior to the accident the petitioner was hale, healthy and she was working as House Keeping at Raksha Hospital and earning Rs.15,000/- per month and due to accidental injuries she is not able to do her job and hence she lost her earning and suffering from mental shock and agony and also facing great financial difficulties. 6. The respondent No.1 being owner of the KSRTC Bus, Respondent No.2 being the RC owner of the Lorry, respondent No.3 being insurer of the Lorry and respondent No.4 is the insurance company of the Lorry are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, this petition was filed against the respondents for claiming compensation. 7. In pursuance to the notice, the respondent No.1 to 4 appeared through their respective counsel and the respondent No.2 and 3 have filed joint written statement and the respondent No.1 and 4 have filed their written statements separately. 8. Brief contents of the written statement of respondent No.1 is that while admitting the ownership of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-3773, this respondent contended that, this accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16/D-9498 as he was parked the Lorry in the middle of the road without any precautionary measurement and signals. Hence, respondent No.2 to 4 are liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner. However, on humanitarian ground this respondent paid the entire hospital bill amounting to Rs.94,059/- and same may be liable to be deducted and in case of holding contributory negligence on the part of the Lorry either fully or partially. The insurer and owner of the lorry shall be directed to refund the medical expenses paid by this respondent to the petitioner to the extent of their liability. Further, it has denied the date, place, mode of accident and nature of injuries, age, income, occupation of the petitioner, medical expenses incurred by her and disability caused to her and also contended that, claim of the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant. Hence, prays to dismiss the petition. 9. Brief contents of the written statement of respondent No.2 and 3 are that the petition filed by the petition is not maintainable neither under facts of the case nor under the question of law and it is to be dismissed in limine. It is further contended that these respondents are the owner and driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16/D-9498 who parked left side of the road and taken the required all safety and precautionary methods with due diligence, because of the negligent and rash driving of the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-3773, this accident was happened and the Bus suddenly came to the footpath and hit the lorry, the driver of the said bus drove the same beyond speed limits in a negligent manner without applying breaks. The petitioner has filed this false case against the respondent No.2 and 3 with malafide intention in view of getting higher compensation and as the respondent No.1 who is the manager of the KSRTC Bus is vicariously liable for the conduct of the bus driver, so, he being solely responsible for the compensation. Hence, prays to dismiss the petition against these respondents. Pushpa vs K.S.R.T.C on 27 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29361503/ 3 10. While admitting about issuance of insurance policy in respect of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16/ D-9498, this respondent restricted its liability to the terms and conditions of the policy. 12. In order to substantiate the case, petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 12 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.12. The petitioner got examined the Doctor by name Dr. Nagaraj B.N. as PW.2 and got marked the 2 documents as Ex.P.13 and P.14. The petitioner claiming the compensation amount of Rs.10,00,000/- with respect to injuries sustained in a road traffic accident. The petitioner produced wound certificate issued by Silicon City Hospital, Hosakote, Bangalore and discharge summary issued by Raksha Multispeciality Hospital, Bangalore and prayed to award compensation amount. The petitioner produced medical bills which is marked as Ex.P.12. Hence, the respondent No.1 and 4 jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
texts.arguments: The respondent No.4 has contended in his written statement that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case and denied the entire averments of the petition. Further contended that, driver of the said vehicle did not possess valid D.L. FC and permit as on the date of the accident and hence, terms and conditions of the insurance policy were violated. It is contended that, this accident occurred due to sole rash and negligent driving of the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-3773, as the driver of Lorry was parked his vehicle with all precautionary measures with signals to other vehicles. Further these respondents denied the date, place and mode of accident, age, income and occupation of the petitioner, medical expenses incurred by her and disability caused to her and also contended that, claim of the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant. Hence, prays to dismiss the petition with costs. 11. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others held that, in the petition for compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the petitioner has to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required. 24. The Petitioner contended that, due to injuries she was suffering from pain and mental agony and she is unable to carry on her day to day activities which she used to do prior to the accident. 25. The Petitioner stated that, at the time of accident she was aged about 52 years and she was working as house keeping work at Raksha Hospital, Bangalore and due to injuries sustained in the accident, she cannot do any work as earlier. The petitioner also sought for expenses towards future medicine for further treatment. In the chief examination affidavit the petitioner deposed that, she is forced to spent another sum of Rs.2,00,000/- for future medication. The petitioner has produced Ex.P.9 estimation report, wherein it is mentioned that the petitioner has been planned for Arthroscopic PCL reconstruction and ACL reconstruction, the approximate cost for the surgery is Rs.2,40,000/-. But PW.2 the Doctor in his cross examination has deposed that the petitioner does not required future treatment. Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head future medical expenditure. 28. The petitioner sustained grievous injuries and took treatment as an inpatient about 8 days. Therefore considering the nature of injury this tribunal has award the amount of Rs.30,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of loss of amenities. 30. Interest: For awarding interest, in MFA.No.103557/2016 (between Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20-03-2018) the Hon'ble High Court of Pushpa vs K.S.R.T.C on 27 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29361503/ 7 Karnataka, held that as per Sec.34 of CPC the rate of interest can be awarded in MVC Cases, cannot be more than 6% p.a.
